messages:
elaine (eng-platform): quick q — we've had a few incidents where product set a feature flag in Console but the rollout policy at runtime routed traffic differently. who should be the source of truth for traffic splits / guards?

mike (eng-runtime): oof yeah i've seen that. runtime enforces guards for safety (cpu/mem, region caps) and can mutate traffic. but console flags are what humans change day-to-day. mismatch = surprise.

sofia (product): can we stop the surprise without blocking product from flipping flags quickly? we need canaries and A/B splits for experiments.

kevin (eng-sre): +1. also need audit trail and alerts when a flag flip causes an automatic guard to trigger fallback. we currently only see latency spikes, not the config collision.

mike (eng-runtime): proposal from runtime: maintain a deterministic precedence table. e.g. runtime safety guards (hard) > rollout policies (platform-controlled soft rules) > feature flags (product). but runtime can be configured to treat console rollout policies as "preferred" if flagged at deploy time.

elaine (eng-platform): i'm wary of a big-footed global rule. easier UX if team ownership is clear: platform owns rollout policies (routing, throttles, region preferences), product owns flags (exposure/experiment tags). precedence should be explicit and visible. we should avoid silent overrides.

sofia (product): make it explicit how a flag interacts with a rollout policy. i.e., a flag can request X% but platform policy might cap it at Y%. product should be notified and see who wins.

mike (eng-runtime): agreed. suggestion: introduce an explicit `precedence` enum on rollout resources: `policy-first`, `flag-first`, `policy-strict`. default = `policy-first` for safety. sample config:```yaml
# per-route rollout config
rollout_policy:
  id: route-analytics-2026-03
  precedence: policy-first   # runtime enforces platform caps before flags
  guards:
    - type: cpu_percent
      max: 75
  splits:
    - model: redwood-alpha
      weight: 80
    - model: redwood-beta
      weight: 20
feature_flag:
  key: experiment/fast-path
  desired_split: 30
```

elaine (eng-platform): nice. UI/Console should surface `precedence` and show a diff whenever someone edits a flag or policy (who changed what + why). also a green/yellow/red indicator when a requested split is reduced by a guard.

devex-bot: docs: https://internal.redwood/docs/rollouts/precedence — new draft RFC (WIP) uploaded. :document:   
sofia (product): for experiments we usually want `flag-first` so product can run short experiments without changing infra. can we allow exceptions at the team level?

mike (eng-runtime): yes, team-level policy overrides possible but must be explicit: `policy-strict` cannot be bypassed. Also need a runtime audit header in responses so apps can attribute decision origin: `x-rollout-source: flag|policy|guard`

kevin (eng-sre): add telemetry: emit an event when desired_split != applied_split with metadata {route, flag, policy_id, reason}. hook this into dashboards/alerts.

elaine (eng-platform): action items: 1) mike to add `precedence` field + `x-rollout-source` header (PR by EOW) 2) devex to add Console UX indicator + diff (track P0) 3) product to list team-level exceptions (sofia) 4) kevin to define telemetry schema for mismatch events. i'll open RFC to lock ownership boundaries.

rollout-bot: created RFC #312: "rollout vs feature-flag precedence and runtime handoff" — link: https://infra/repo/rfcs/312  (assigned: elaine) :white_check_mark:

sofia (product): thanks all — feel better about this. please cc product on the PRs so we can validate experiment flows. :thumbsup:

mike (eng-runtime): will do. small note: we should also add a grace period where a flag flip can be staged and validated against policy changes to avoid flip-flapping.

elaine (eng-platform): noted. adding to RFC. closing thread for now, continuing in RFC comments.
